q: Four matrices have dimensions 10 × 20, 20 × 5, 5 × 30 and 30 × 10. What is the minimum number of scalar multiplications needed to compute their product?
For the chain p = [6, 2, 10, 3, 8] (four matrices), what is the minimum multiplication cost?
How many different full parenthesisations does a product of 5 matrices have?
explain: The count is the Catalan number C₄ = (1/5)·C(8, 4) = 70/5 = 14. In general, n matrices have C_{n−1} bracketings, which grows exponentially. That is why trying them all is hopeless, and DP is needed.

q: Which statements about dynamic programming are correct?
options: Bottom-up tabulation and top-down memoisation compute the same values
DP is useful only when subproblems overlap
Merge sort is a dynamic-programming algorithm because it reuses subproblem results
explain:
(A): they are two schedules for the same recurrence. (B): without overlap there is nothing to reuse. (C): the m and s tables are n × n.

(D) is false: merge sort's subproblems are disjoint, so it is divide and conquer and stores nothing for reuse.
